overview.text: The Eastern Fox Snake is a harmless rat snake of the upper Midwest of the United States and southern Ontario.

identification.text: Light golden brown with dark brown spots, a yellow checkerboard belly and a short, flattened snout.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 3 to 6 ft (0.9 to 1.8 m) long.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: East of the Mississippi River: Wisconsin, Illinois, eastern Missouri, Indiana, Michigan and Ohio, and southern Ontario. Its close relative, the Western Fox Snake, lives west of the river.

habitat.text: Open woodland, prairie, farmland, pasture and marshes.

behaviour.text: A strong climber, but usually on the ground. Active by day, sometimes hunting at night in hot summers.

recognise.text: Golden brown with dark brown spots.
